scope: Dreamcast VMU and GameCube raw-card formats, isolated emulator launch paths and safe file copying

checks: New VMU: native 128 KiB image and 200 free save blocks
New GameCube card: native 16 Mbit image and 251 free save blocks
Native filesystem directories, checksums, redundant metadata and bounded allocation chains
Selected VMU files retain original payloads; missing files, duplicate names and insufficient space are rejected
Session-private firmware, VMUs and core options leave global files unchanged
Disabled VMU expansion slots do not become attached because an old file exists
Dolphin native region filenames are the exact paths tracked by cloud sync
Unknown compressed GameCube regions require an unmanaged launch fallback

dreamcast.verified_by: Native Dreamcast BIOS File manager running inside Flycast on a private Xvfb display
dreamcast.observed: A-1 shows 185 Free and PSOV2/MAIN_DATA using 15 blocks

gamecube.verified_by: Dolphin GameCube Memory Card Manager calls its native GCMemcard::Open filesystem validator
gamecube.observed: Slot A opens without error and displays Free Blocks: 251, Free Files: 127

limitations: Changing raw files under a running Flycast or Dolphin process is not a verified card swap; selections apply at next launch.
The native GameCube format was verified by Dolphin's own card manager; the separate PSO cold boot did not reach a reliable save-write check.
GameCube saves that bind to a card serial must retain that raw image identity; selective GameCube save transfer is not implemented here.
Live Flycast option reconnect is present in upstream core source, but the installed Spark RetroArch lacks the required network command; no operator runtime was used to test it.
